metadata.title: How much time do adults spend on the PIAAC assessment and why does it matter?

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The analysis uses PIAAC computer-based assessment log files, restricted to participants assigned to the literacy and numeracy modules. The note in the figure captions indicates the sample is limited to those module-assigned respondents, but the excerpt does not report the specific sampling/replicate weight variables or whether complex survey weights were applied in the timing and disengagement computations. Because the paper focuses on descriptive timing indicators (total time on task, item-level time percentiles, and T-disengagement rates) rather than PV-based achievement modeling, the weighting strategy is primarily relevant for producing population-representative estimates of time and disengagement at the individual and country levels. Analysts should apply the PIAAC survey weights from the Data Explorer/IDB (and replicate weights if used) when available to account for the multistage sampling design and to ensure valid cross-country comparisons.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This OECD brief analyzes log-file timing indicators (e.g., total time on task, time percentiles, and T-disengagement thresholds) rather than cognitive achievement scores based on PIAAC plausible values. Plausible values are therefore not applicable to the reported dependent measures because the outcomes are behavioral/timing constructs derived from timestamps and item-level response behavior. Missing-data handling is not reported in the excerpt because the paper does not describe an imputation/deletion procedure for incomplete log records or item-level timing gaps; this is a reporting gap for transparency, though the computations are based on log events for module-assigned participants.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The sample includes only participants to the computer-based assessment who were assigned to the literacy and numeracy modules (as stated in the figure notes). The excerpt does not specify additional exclusions (e.g., minimum log completeness, missing covariates, or outlier trimming) beyond the module-assignment restriction.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD brief uses PIAAC computer-based assessment log files to study how much time adults spend on literacy and numeracy tasks, and how timing relates to item difficulty and disengagement. The analysis is restricted to participants assigned to the literacy and numeracy modules and reports descriptive cross-country differences in total time on task (e.g., about 50 minutes on average in Austria, Finland, Germany, and Norway; about 40 minutes in Ireland, Italy, Slovakia, Spain, and the UK). Because PIAAC is adaptive, the paper also discusses an item-level time percentile approach to account for differing item assignments across respondents, noting that this has little effect on country rankings. It further reports that higher education and older age are associated with longer time, while greater ICT familiarity is associated with less time and gender differences are small. Finally, it defines T-disengagement using a minimum time threshold per item and shows substantial cross-country variation in disengagement rates, with disengagement more prevalent in the second half of the assessment. The excerpt does not report PV handling or missing-data procedures because the outcomes are timing/engagement indicators derived from timestamps rather than PV-based achievement scores.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD descriptive analysis of PIAAC log-file timing and disengagement indicators rather than an empirical ML prediction study. As a result, there is no ML model training/evaluation, no PV-based achievement target, and no reported sample size or per-country Ns in the provided excerpt; the extraction therefore leaves total_students and n_students as null. The paper still provides substantive cross-country results (time-on-task and T-disengagement rates) but does not fit the schema’s ML main_findings structure.
